clinician.trajectory_summary: A woman in her 20s presented to plastic surgery clinic with a 4-month history of progressive right posterior scalp swelling associated with pruritus and intermittent discomfort. Physical examination revealed two distinct right parieto-occipital lesions: a 12mm subcutaneous mobile tender cystic lesion with intact skin, and an 11mm erythematous lesion with irregular borders and brown discolouration. The patient denied systemic symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss, bleeding). Initial biopsy (E002) demonstrated a basaloid cutaneous lesion on H&E consistent with adenoid cystic carcinoma, with immunohistochemistry showing patchy positive staining for epithelial membrane antigen (apical aspect of pseudo glandular cyst) and diffuse positive staining for pan-cytokeratin (AE1/AE3). PET-CT imaging (E003) revealed absence of FDG uptake or hypermetabolic activity in lymph nodes, organs, and bone marrow, supporting a primary cutaneous origin rather than metastatic disease from salivary glands. Complete surgical excision of both lesions was performed under local anesthesia (E004) with reconstruction using a rotational flap. Histopathological examination of the excised tissue confirmed the diagnosis of PCACC.
